summary: Testing whether the same held-proposal harm arises through joint consensus, which is the normal route for multi-node changes. The successor keeps every invocation case and instead routes the removal through a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointImplicit carrying remove node 3, so the member is a voter in the outgoing half while the config is joint and is dropped from both halves only when raft itself proposes the leave-joint entry. The harness records that transition as removal_applied with the applied conf-change entry count and the observed voter and outgoing fields, and that event is now a prerequisite of the witness admission, so the witness comparisons rest on a joint-consensus removal rather than a simple one. A local run in the scratch copy shows the joint route behaves as the source predicts and the harm follows: node 3 ends outside both halves with voter false and outgoing false after applying one conf-change entry carrying the removal, and after the re-add with leader 1 still unchanged the witness invocation returned false at 1201 ms, the context-free invocation stayed pending through its 2000 ms window, the configuration proposal returned false at 800 ms, the never-removed member committed throughout, and the post-leader-change invocation returned true. Fifteen invocation comparisons plus the two administrative ones are unchanged; the new prerequisite adds the trigger evidence. Remaining budget is healthy at roughly fifty minutes and thirty-five executions.
